## Purpose

Part of #62051 (the truncated/unclosed-parameter rows only; the block with no invoke, the cut inside a tool name, and the V4 spellings are not addressed here, so the issue should stay open) and extends the `arg_value_extender` incremental streaming architecture (introduced for `qwen3_xml` in #62027 and `minimax_m2` in #62035) to the DeepSeek DSML parsers (`deepseek_v32`, `deepseek_v4`, and `deepseek_v41`).

### Problem (#62051)
1. **Unclosed / Truncated DSML Parameters Produce Invalid JSON on Stream Flush**:
   - In `_dsml_args_to_json(raw_args, partial)`, trailing unclosed `<｜DSML｜parameter name="..." string="...">...` tags were matched via `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE` **only when `partial=True`**.
   - When `partial=False` (called during `extract_tool_calls(...)` or during `_flush_arg_converter()` at `</｜DSML｜invoke>` / `finish_streaming()`), `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE` was skipped.
   - As a result:
     - **Case 1 (Truncated at `max_tokens`)**: During streaming, `converter(raw_args, True)` emitted `{"url": "https://example.com` (`prev_converted_len > 0`). On `finish_streaming()`, `_flush_arg_converter()` called `converter(raw_args, False)` which returned `"{}"` (length 2 < `prev_converted_len`), so no closing `"}` delta was emitted—leaving clients with invalid, unclosed JSON (`{"url": "https://example.com`).
     - **Case 4 (Model omits `</｜DSML｜parameter>` before `</｜DSML｜invoke>`)**: Non-streaming `extract_tool_calls` dropped the parameter (`{}`), while streaming emitted unclosed JSON (`{"file_path": "/tmp/a`).
2. **Quadratic Re-conversion of Long DSML Tool Arguments**:
   - Unlike `Qwen3Parser` (#62027) and `MinimaxM2Parser` (#62035), DeepSeek DSML parsers lacked an `arg_value_extender` and re-ran full regex conversion over `slot.args` whenever `>` appeared inside streamed argument content (e.g., code, HTML, shell redirects, markdown).

### Solution
1. **Consistent Unclosed Parameter Recovery + Partial Tag Holdback**:
   - Extract `_dsml_parse_args` so trailing unclosed `<｜DSML｜parameter ...>` blocks at the end of `raw_args` are recovered in both `partial=True` and `partial=False`.
   - Add `_value_end_window(text, value_end_re)` using `regex.fullmatch(..., partial=True)` against `</｜DSML｜parameter>|<｜DSML｜parameter\s+name=` so any trailing suffix of an open parameter value that could still complete into a closing or sibling parameter tag is held back during `partial=True` streaming (since `DeepSeekV4Parser` has no lexer transitions on `PARAM_START`/`PARAM_CLOSE` in `TOOL_ARGS`).
   - Hold back `_unwrap_wrapper_args` when `partial=True` and a single `arguments`/`input` wrapper parameter contains an incomplete JSON string, preventing premature streaming of `"arguments": ` before unwrapping.
2. **Incremental DSML String Argument Streaming (`_dsml_arg_value_extender`)**:
   - Implement `_dsml_arg_value_extender` for `deepseek_v4`, `deepseek_v41`, and `deepseek_v32`, streaming open `string="true"` DSML parameter values in $O(1)$ conversions with respect to argument length (reducing partial converter calls on a 200-line `write_file` call from 206 to 6).

## Test Plan

- Added `TestArgValueExtender` in `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py` (long 200-line DSML call with `>`, `<`, quotes, backslashes, and partial DSML tag lookalikes; $O(1)$ conversion count verification; #62051 truncated & unclosed parameter streaming/non-streaming parity).
- Added parametrized streaming and non-streaming tests for truncated and unclosed parameters in `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py` and `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v32.py`.
- All 279 tests in `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v32.py`, `test_deepseek_v4.py`, `test_deepseek_v41.py`, and `test_parser_engine.py` pass.

### Credits & Acknowledgments
- Credit to **@robertgshaw2-redhat** for reporting #62051 and providing the DSML truncation/unclosed-parameter reproduction cases, and to **@YaashuDave** for reproducing all five cases and analyzing `StreamingParserEngine.finish()` on #62051.
- Credit to **@deadstrobe5** (#62027, #62035) for designing the `ArgValueExtender` incremental argument streaming architecture in `ParserEngine`, and **@jayzuccarelli** (#58780) for prior work on incremental DeepSeek V3.2/V4 tool argument streaming.
- Special thanks to **@JohnZhao01** (#62290) and **@smiyamoto3** for end-to-end validation, edge-case reproductions, and review feedback on this PR.

🚀

Thanks for this fix. We ran it end to end on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with the Python frontend and wanted to share the results: it clearly helps, and we found two things that may be worth a look.

**Setup**

- Image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-1b2a666391f2a24228a1436b64d547c34cc6b6ce`, which is 4 commits after this PR's base (`da9134bc`); the three `vllm/parser/deepseek_v*.py` files are identical to the base. We applied the PR head `afa41800` by replacing those three files.
- `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, 4×H200, TP4, `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0`, `--tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41`.
- 286 requests per build, the same set for both: one `get_weather` tool whose `city` value the prompt makes long, cut by `max_tokens` (20–320, thinking off and on) or by a stop string (`</｜DSML｜ parameter>` / `</｜DSML｜ invoke>`); stream and non-stream; greedy and sampled.

**1. The new V4.1 test fails as written (6 cases)**

`test_truncated_and_unclosed_parameter_streaming_and_non_streaming` in `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py` sends no tools, so the tool parser is not enabled and both calls come back empty (`ParseOutput(reasoning='', content='', tool_calls=[])`). The other tests in that file pass `tools=DUMMY_TOOLS`. With this change all 151 tests in the three files pass, and the fixed V4.1 test fails on the base files (7 failures), so it does cover the change:

```diff
@@ -184,6 +184,7 @@
             tokens,
             chunk_size=chunk_size,
             finished_on_last=True,
+            tools=DUMMY_TOOLS,
         )
     )
     assert len(output.tool_calls) == 1
@@ -193,7 +194,7 @@
     parser_non_stream = parser_for(tokenizer, {"thinking": False})
     _, content, calls = parser_non_stream.parse(
         text,
-        _test_request(),
+        _test_request(tools=DUMMY_TOOLS),
         enable_auto_tools=True,
         model_output_token_ids=[tid for tid, _ in tokens],
     )
```

The existing tests in all three files also pass with the PR applied (140/140).

**2. End-to-end: arguments of truncated tool calls**

| | base nightly | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| calls cut by `max_tokens`: invalid JSON | 14 / 49 | 0 / 47 |
| calls cut by `max_tokens`: `{}` | 29 / 49 | 15 / 47 |
| calls cut by `max_tokens`: clean partial `city` value | 6 / 49 | 20 / 47 |
| calls cut by a stop string: invalid JSON or `{}` | 13 / 30 | 0 / 28 |

`finish_reason` is `length` for every call cut by `max_tokens` on both builds (since #59324), so clients can tell these calls are incomplete. The remaining `{}` all come from small budgets (20–80 tokens); we did not capture the raw text, but they look like cuts before the first parameter value started. 3 more calls were cut right after the parameter head and returned `{"city": ""}`. No server errors in either run.

**3. A partial close marker stays in the value**

9 of the 47 truncated calls with this PR returned values such as `"Paris</｜DSML｜ parameter"` or `"Paris</"`: the generation was cut inside `</｜DSML｜ parameter>`. A unit repro with the V4.1 harness: cut `...string="true">Paris` after each prefix of the close marker (`<`, `</`, `</｜`, `</｜DSML｜`, `</｜DSML｜ parameter`). Each of these returns the fragment in the value, in streaming (chunk 1 / 7 / 10000) and non-streaming.

`_dsml_parse_args` trims the trailing value-end window only when `partial=True`, and the final conversion at the end of the output uses `partial=False`. Trimming the unclosed trailing parameter in both cases fixes all five cut points (streaming and non-streaming), and the 151 tests still pass:

```diff
     pm = partial_param_re.search(raw_args, last_end)
     if pm:
         name, is_str, value = pm.group(1), pm.group(2), pm.group(3)
-        if partial:
-            window = _value_end_window(value, value_end_re)
-            if window:
-                value = value[: -len(window)]
+        # The trailing parameter is unclosed: a suffix that can only be the start of its close
+        # marker (or of the next parameter) is not part of the value, also at the end of the output.
+        window = _value_end_window(value, value_end_re)
+        if window:
+            value = value[: -len(window)]
```

This drops a value that genuinely ends in a lone `<` when the output is cut right there, which seems acceptable for a value that is already truncated. We have only checked this change with unit tests, not end to end. Happy to share the repro script if useful.

**4. Out of scope, for reference**

When the cut lands inside the `<｜DSML｜ calls>` opener, the partial opener (`<｜DSML｜`) is returned as content (1 / 286 with this PR, 4 / 286 on the base). This PR does not change that path. The Rust frontend side of truncated DSML calls is handled separately in #62290; that PR does not touch the Python parsers.

@JohnZhao01 thanks a lot for the end-to-end run and the detailed numbers. Both points are addressed in 2b2c4b2:

1. **V4.1 test sends no tools.** `test_truncated_and_unclosed_parameter_streaming_and_non_streaming` now passes `tools=DUMMY_TOOLS` to both the streaming replay and `_test_request(...)`, so the tool parser is actually exercised.
2. **Partial close marker kept in the value.** `_dsml_parse_args` now trims the value-end window of the unclosed trailing parameter on both paths (`partial=True` and the final `partial=False` conversion), as you suggested. I added `test_python_argument_conversion_drops_partial_close_marker`, which covers your five cut points (`<`, `</`, `</｜`, `</｜DSML｜`, `</｜DSML｜ parameter`) with `partial` both `True` and `False`. Before the change, the `partial=False` conversion returned the fragment for all five, e.g. `"Paris</｜DSML｜ parameter"`; after the change, all return `{"city": "Paris"}`. A genuine `<` inside a value that cannot start a marker (the existing `"  a<b"` case) is still preserved.

Agreed on (4): the partial `<｜DSML｜ calls>` opener leaking as content is a separate path, so I left it out of this PR.

Note on local verification: my machine can't build the full vLLM test environment, so I checked the parsing logic in isolation and ran `ruff`. The full `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v*.py` run in CI would be appreciated.

@smiyamoto3 thanks for testing on main and for the precise repro. Addressed in e235cf8:

- **Repeated parameter name.** `_dsml_parse_args` now skips the trailing-parameter recovery when the unclosed parameter's name is already in `params`, using your suggested change. For `...name="city" string="true">Paris</｜DSML｜ parameter>...name="city" string="true">Lyon`, partial and final conversion now both give `{"city": "Paris"}`, matching main. Replaying that string one character at a time, every partial conversion after the first close stays `{"city": "Paris"}`, so the stream terminates cleanly. Before, it moved to `"L"`, `"Ly"`, … and ended at `{"city": "Lyon"}`. I added `test_python_argument_conversion_ignores_unclosed_repeated_name` (partial and final). Non-string values had the same problem (`n=1` followed by an unclosed `n=2`) and are covered by the same fix.
- **Description.** It now says `Part of #62051` and lists the rows this PR does not address (no invoke, a cut inside the tool name, the V4 spellings).
- **#58780 nit.** Agreed. Whichever lands first, I'll rebase `_dsml_arg_value_extender` on it here if this one is second.

As before, I could only check the parsing logic in isolation and run `ruff` on my machine. I haven't run the full engine test files locally, so CI or your rebased run would be appreciated.

@deep1blue Thanks for the update. Could you run `pre-commit run ruff-format --files tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v*.py`? It reformats two of the test files. The repeated name is fixed in both paths and the deepseek engine tests pass on my rebased run, so LGTM after that.
@smiyamoto3 done in 13bccc8 (`ruff format tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v*.py` reformatted `test_deepseek_v32.py` and `test_deepseek_v4.py`). Thanks for the review!

Thank you very much @smiyamoto3 for the thorough review, rebased test run, and formal **`APPROVED`** sign-off ([#pullrequestreview-5564228984](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62259#pullrequestreview-5564228984)), and thank you again @JohnZhao01 for the end-to-end 4×H200 `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` validation ([#issuecomment-6251722905](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62259#issuecomment-6251722905), showing invalid-JSON truncated tool calls dropping from 28.6% / 43.3% to 0%)!

Gentle ping @sfeng33 @chaunceyjiang @bbrowning @aarnphm @WoosukKwon @DarkLight1337 — since this has been independently validated end-to-end on 4×H200 and approved by @smiyamoto3, would you mind taking a quick look for maintainer approval / CI trigger when you have a moment? Thank you so much for your time!

Thanks for picking up the close-marker trim and the test fix so quickly. We re-ran the current head (`13bccc83`) end to end on the same setup as above (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 4×H200, Python frontend, nightly `1b2a6663`, the same 286 requests), and it looks good:

| calls cut by `max_tokens` | base nightly | current head (`13bccc83`) |
|---|---|---|
| partial close marker in the value | 0 / 49 | 0 / 49 |
| invalid JSON arguments | 14 / 49 | 0 / 49 |
| clean partial `city` value | 6 / 49 | 29 / 49 |
| `{"city": ""}` | 0 / 49 | 4 / 49 |
| `{}` | 29 / 49 | 16 / 49 |

All calls cut by a stop string come back clean (33/33), there are no server errors, and all 163 tests in the three DeepSeek test files pass.

To see where the cuts land, we recovered the raw generated text from the chat `logprobs` in a separate run of 56 requests on the same build. In that run (a different set of calls from the table), every `{}` call (4 of them) was cut before the first parameter value started, and every `{"city": ""}` call (also 4) was cut right after the parameter's opening tag, before any value text, so both results are expected. The calls in the table above were not individually checked against the raw text.

@JohnZhao01 thank you so much for re-running the full validation on `13bccc83`, both the 286-request suite on 4×H200 (`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, Python frontend) and the separate 56-request run with chat `logprobs`. Very helpful to see the result on hardware:

- calls cut by `max_tokens`: 0/49 with a partial close marker, 0/49 with invalid JSON, 29/49 with a clean partial `city` value
- calls cut by a stop string: 33/33 clean
- 163/163 tests in the three DeepSeek test files passing

Thanks also for using the raw text to trace the remaining `{}` and `{"city": ""}` results to cuts before the first value and right after the opening tag — that matches what the parser should emit for those cut points.

If everything looks good on your end now, would you mind also leaving a quick approving review (`Files changed` → `Review changes` → `Approve`) so maintainers can see both yours and @smiyamoto3's sign-offs at a glance? Really appreciate all your testing!

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

I think this is the right direction. The invalid JSON from #62051 is gone here: a value cut by `max_tokens` streams `{"url": "https://x.com/a?b="}` where main streams `{"url": "`. Tested at 2b2c4b2 rebased on main, where the three deepseek engine files pass, including at different delta sizes.

On the other hand, two parameters with the same name leave the streamed arguments unterminated: `...name="city" string="true">Paris</｜DSML｜parameter>...name="city" string="true">Lyon` streams `{"city": "Paris` while non-streaming returns `{"city": "Lyon"}`; main gives `{"city": "Paris"}` both ways. Skipping the recovery for an already closed name brings it back, with those files still green:

```diff
     pm = partial_param_re.search(raw_args, last_end)
+    if pm and pm.group(1) in params:
+        pm = None
     if pm:
```

The other rows of #62051 look unchanged (the block with no invoke, the cut inside a tool name, the V4 spellings). Could the description say `Part of #62051`, so merging this keeps the issue open for those?

nit: Whichever of this and #58780 lands second will have to redo `_dsml_arg_value_extender`.
Thanks for the quick fix. LGTM.

Re-validated the current head (`13bccc83`) end to end on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with the Python frontend (details in the comment above): no invalid JSON or partial close markers in truncated calls, and the DeepSeek parser tests pass. LGTM.

 class TestMissingFunctionCallsWrapper:

🚀

Thanks for this fix. We ran it end to end on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with the Python frontend and wanted to share the results: it clearly helps, and we found two things that may be worth a look.

**Setup**

- Image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-1b2a666391f2a24228a1436b64d547c34cc6b6ce`, which is 4 commits after this PR's base (`da9134bc`); the three `vllm/parser/deepseek_v*.py` files are identical to the base. We applied the PR head `afa41800` by replacing those three files.
- `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, 4×H200, TP4, `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0`, `--tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41`.
- 286 requests per build, the same set for both: one `get_weather` tool whose `city` value the prompt makes long, cut by `max_tokens` (20–320, thinking off and on) or by a stop string (`</｜DSML｜ parameter>` / `</｜DSML｜ invoke>`); stream and non-stream; greedy and sampled.

**1. The new V4.1 test fails as written (6 cases)**

`test_truncated_and_unclosed_parameter_streaming_and_non_streaming` in `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py` sends no tools, so the tool parser is not enabled and both calls come back empty (`ParseOutput(reasoning='', content='', tool_calls=[])`). The other tests in that file pass `tools=DUMMY_TOOLS`. With this change all 151 tests in the three files pass, and the fixed V4.1 test fails on the base files (7 failures), so it does cover the change:

```diff
@@ -184,6 +184,7 @@
             tokens,
             chunk_size=chunk_size,
             finished_on_last=True,
+            tools=DUMMY_TOOLS,
         )
     )
     assert len(output.tool_calls) == 1
@@ -193,7 +194,7 @@
     parser_non_stream = parser_for(tokenizer, {"thinking": False})
     _, content, calls = parser_non_stream.parse(
         text,
-        _test_request(),
+        _test_request(tools=DUMMY_TOOLS),
         enable_auto_tools=True,
         model_output_token_ids=[tid for tid, _ in tokens],
     )
```

The existing tests in all three files also pass with the PR applied (140/140).

**2. End-to-end: arguments of truncated tool calls**

| | base nightly | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| calls cut by `max_tokens`: invalid JSON | 14 / 49 | 0 / 47 |
| calls cut by `max_tokens`: `{}` | 29 / 49 | 15 / 47 |
| calls cut by `max_tokens`: clean partial `city` value | 6 / 49 | 20 / 47 |
| calls cut by a stop string: invalid JSON or `{}` | 13 / 30 | 0 / 28 |

`finish_reason` is `length` for every call cut by `max_tokens` on both builds (since #59324), so clients can tell these calls are incomplete. The remaining `{}` all come from small budgets (20–80 tokens); we did not capture the raw text, but they look like cuts before the first parameter value started. 3 more calls were cut right after the parameter head and returned `{"city": ""}`. No server errors in either run.

**3. A partial close marker stays in the value**

9 of the 47 truncated calls with this PR returned values such as `"Paris</｜DSML｜ parameter"` or `"Paris</"`: the generation was cut inside `</｜DSML｜ parameter>`. A unit repro with the V4.1 harness: cut `...string="true">Paris` after each prefix of the close marker (`<`, `</`, `</｜`, `</｜DSML｜`, `</｜DSML｜ parameter`). Each of these returns the fragment in the value, in streaming (chunk 1 / 7 / 10000) and non-streaming.

`_dsml_parse_args` trims the trailing value-end window only when `partial=True`, and the final conversion at the end of the output uses `partial=False`. Trimming the unclosed trailing parameter in both cases fixes all five cut points (streaming and non-streaming), and the 151 tests still pass:

```diff
     pm = partial_param_re.search(raw_args, last_end)
     if pm:
         name, is_str, value = pm.group(1), pm.group(2), pm.group(3)
-        if partial:
-            window = _value_end_window(value, value_end_re)
-            if window:
-                value = value[: -len(window)]
+        # The trailing parameter is unclosed: a suffix that can only be the start of its close
+        # marker (or of the next parameter) is not part of the value, also at the end of the output.
+        window = _value_end_window(value, value_end_re)
+        if window:
+            value = value[: -len(window)]
```

This drops a value that genuinely ends in a lone `<` when the output is cut right there, which seems acceptable for a value that is already truncated. We have only checked this change with unit tests, not end to end. Happy to share the repro script if useful.

**4. Out of scope, for reference**

When the cut lands inside the `<｜DSML｜ calls>` opener, the partial opener (`<｜DSML｜`) is returned as content (1 / 286 with this PR, 4 / 286 on the base). This PR does not change that path. The Rust frontend side of truncated DSML calls is handled separately in #62290; that PR does not touch the Python parsers.

@JohnZhao01 thanks a lot for the end-to-end run and the detailed numbers. Both points are addressed in 2b2c4b2:

1. **V4.1 test sends no tools.** `test_truncated_and_unclosed_parameter_streaming_and_non_streaming` now passes `tools=DUMMY_TOOLS` to both the streaming replay and `_test_request(...)`, so the tool parser is actually exercised.
2. **Partial close marker kept in the value.** `_dsml_parse_args` now trims the value-end window of the unclosed trailing parameter on both paths (`partial=True` and the final `partial=False` conversion), as you suggested. I added `test_python_argument_conversion_drops_partial_close_marker`, which covers your five cut points (`<`, `</`, `</｜`, `</｜DSML｜`, `</｜DSML｜ parameter`) with `partial` both `True` and `False`. Before the change, the `partial=False` conversion returned the fragment for all five, e.g. `"Paris</｜DSML｜ parameter"`; after the change, all return `{"city": "Paris"}`. A genuine `<` inside a value that cannot start a marker (the existing `"  a<b"` case) is still preserved.

Agreed on (4): the partial `<｜DSML｜ calls>` opener leaking as content is a separate path, so I left it out of this PR.

Note on local verification: my machine can't build the full vLLM test environment, so I checked the parsing logic in isolation and ran `ruff`. The full `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v*.py` run in CI would be appreciated.

@smiyamoto3 thanks for testing on main and for the precise repro. Addressed in e235cf8:

- **Repeated parameter name.** `_dsml_parse_args` now skips the trailing-parameter recovery when the unclosed parameter's name is already in `params`, using your suggested change. For `...name="city" string="true">Paris</｜DSML｜ parameter>...name="city" string="true">Lyon`, partial and final conversion now both give `{"city": "Paris"}`, matching main. Replaying that string one character at a time, every partial conversion after the first close stays `{"city": "Paris"}`, so the stream terminates cleanly. Before, it moved to `"L"`, `"Ly"`, … and ended at `{"city": "Lyon"}`. I added `test_python_argument_conversion_ignores_unclosed_repeated_name` (partial and final).
